Require a permission in an action handler

Source: R/permissions.R
aa_require.Rd

Call it on the first line of a handler. If the user has the permission, it returns TRUE. If not, it reports an access_denied event to the on_event hook (the permission name goes into value), shows the user a notification and quietly aborts the handler through shiny::req().

Usage

aa_require(
  auth,
  permission,
  provider,
  on_event = NULL,
  settings = aa_settings(),
  session_id = NULL
)

Arguments

auth

The authorization object (a list with a reactive user value, as returned by the login module) or the user itself (a list with login and role).

permission

Permission name.

provider

Permission provider, see aa_can().

on_event

Event hook function(event, user, session_id, value) or NULL.

settings

Settings, the result of aa_settings() (language of the denial text).

session_id

Session identifier for the hook. By default it is taken from the current Shiny session.

Value

Invisibly TRUE. If the permission is missing, aborts the handler.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
observeEvent(input$run_task, {
  aa_require(auth, "Run", provider, on_event = log_event)
  # ... the action ...
})
} # }
